worst_places.quote: The Mediator pattern (a GRASP pattern) encapsulates how a set of objects interact by introducing a mediator object that handles their communication.
worst_places.problem: quiz-20 states as fact that Mediator is a GRASP pattern. It is not. The site's own article content/topics/oop-patterns/en/02-grasp-patterns.md lists exactly seven GRASP patterns (Information Expert, Creator, Controller, Low Coupling, High Cohesion, Polymorphism, Pure Fabrication) and Mediator is documented in content/topics/oop-patterns/en/05-behavioral-patterns.md as a GoF behavioral pattern. The item then demotes 'Low Coupling' — which IS a real GRASP pattern — to 'just a principle' and marks it wrong. The item teaches the reader a false taxonomy and marks the true GRASP answer as the distractor.
worst_places.before: Which GRASP pattern is applied when you create a Mediator object to handle communication between multiple complex subsystems, reducing direct dependencies between them? / correct: Mediator — centralizes control logic and communication
worst_places.after: Which GRASP pattern does a mediator object apply when it sits between several subsystems so they stop referencing each other directly? / correct: Indirection — an intermediate object mediates, so neither side holds a reference to the other. Explanation: 'Mediator is the GoF pattern; the GRASP pattern it applies is Indirection. Low Coupling is the goal Indirection serves, Creator is about who calls `new`, Expert is about who owns the data.'

worst_places.before: The senior-level nuance is that IoC isn't one specific tool — a full DI container (like `tsyringe` or `InversifyJS`), a plain object passed as a constructor argument (as above), or React Context all implement the same principle: someone other than the consumer decides which concrete implementation to supply, and that decision point (the "composition root") is pushed to the single outermost layer of the app rather than scattered through every component that happens to need a service.
worst_places.after: The nuance seniors are expected to know: IoC is not one specific tool. A full dependency injection (DI) container like `tsyringe` or `InversifyJS` implements it. So does a plain object passed as a constructor argument, as above. So does React Context. All three do the same thing: someone other than the consumer picks the concrete implementation. That decision lives in one place — the "composition root", the outermost layer of the app. Without it, the choice is scattered across every component that needs a service.

patterns: The quiz is answerable without reading it. correctIndex is 0 in 20/24 and never 2 or 3 (guessing A scores 83%), and the correct option is the longest of the four in 15/24 en / 17/24 ru because only the correct option carries a trailing '— because ...' clause. This is the third quiz bank in a row with exactly this shape (quiz/oop-patterns: 18/25 at index 0, 22/25 longest-correct), so it is a generator default, not a per-file accident: fix it once in the generation template, not item by item.

The quiz was assembled from per-language generation batches that were never read end to end. The tells cluster: 8/24 items (quiz-11/12/14/15 `java`, quiz-22/23/24/25 `typescript`) have the language tag with no ``` fence in BOTH locales, so the code renders as raw prose; four of them are Java on a Node/React site; id `solid-grasp-quiz-21` is missing from a 1-25 range; quiz-12's stem still opens 'Consider a payment processing system' above a Rectangle/Shape example; quiz-25's distractor still says 'errors that Rectangle doesn't'. Item content duplicates in blocks too — 4 near-identical SRP items (1, 6, 11, 16), 4 DIP-inject-an-interface items (9, 14, 18, 24), 3 ISP forced-stub items (13, 19, 25), and the same Square/Rectangle LSP question twice (12 in Java, 23 in TypeScript).

The quiz contradicts the site's own theory and itself on GRASP taxonomy. quiz-20 asserts Mediator is a GRASP pattern (the article 02-grasp-patterns.md lists seven, Mediator is not among them; 05-behavioral-patterns.md documents it as GoF) and marks the real GRASP answer 'Low Coupling' wrong; quiz-5 marks non-GRASP Factory correct in a GRASP question with Creator wrong; quiz-8 then says 'Factory (Creator)' are the same thing. Meanwhile the QUESTION bank gets all of this right and goes further than the article (it covers Indirection and Protected Variations, which 02-grasp-patterns.md does not). The two files in one zone teach different facts.

The question bank is the opposite problem: excellent, internally consistent, senior-level content trapped in over-long single sentences. 57.8% of en sentences exceed 25 words vs 39% ru, so the English is measurably harder than the Russian for the same content. The structural habit is one long sentence carrying a definition plus a parenthetical list plus a contrast clause, all joined by an em-dash — the fix is mechanical (split at the em-dash and the colon) and does not touch a single technical claim.

The Russian question bank leaves the load-bearing vocabulary in English. «Trade-off» is untranslated in all 25 entries, plus `actor'у/actor'ам/actor'а/actor'ов` (English noun + Russian case ending via apostrophe, q-1/q-8/q-21), `failure mode` (q-7, q-13), «коллабораторами» (q-6/q-19/q-25) and «заботы» as a calque of "concerns" (7×). q-21 additionally contains an ungrammatical machine-translation seam («превращает корень агрегата в разбитые на валидатор...»).
notes: Overlap with questions/oop-patterns.json is near zero, not high: 0 of its 34 entries mention SOLID, GRASP, or any of the five principles by name — it is pure GoF (Singleton, Builder, Decorator, Observer, Command, Bridge, Facade, Proxy, Flyweight, State, Mediator, Null Object...). Only 2 of solid-grasp's 25 overlap: q-9 Factory Method (vs oop-patterns q-2/q-11) and q-10 Adapter (vs q-18). Verdict: keep them as two banks. The real problem is the opposite of duplication — solid-grasp's 25 excellent questions are the ONLY SOLID/GRASP practice on the site, and the articles that explain the theory (topics/oop-patterns/*/01-solid-principles.md, 02-grasp-patterns.md, rated 4-5 by the oop-patterns audit) sit behind a different page the reader never visits. Suggest surfacing those two articles from the solid-grasp page; if that is not possible, the acronym expansions in the quiz stop being optional. Also worth noting: the solid-grasp question bank covers Indirection and Protected Variations, which 02-grasp-patterns.md does not — so the article should gain those two sections rather than the bank losing them.
